sights.w: Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 645) — through the Kaminarimon thunder gate and the Nakamise-dōri stall street to the main hall and five-storey pagoda.

sights.n: Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館)
sights.w: Japan's oldest and largest museum — 120,000 objects including 89 National Treasures, from Jōmon pottery to samurai armour and ukiyo-e, in Ueno Park.
Japan's first public park (1873) — museums, the zoo, Shinobazu Pond's lotus beds, Tōshō-gū and Tokyo's most famous cherry-blossom avenue. Free entry.
'Kitchen Town' — some 170 shops between Ueno and Asakusa selling knives, lacquerware, noren and the plastic food samples of every Japanese shop window.
The national sumo hall — three of the six annual grand tournaments (January, May, September) are fought here; the Sumo Museum and the chanko-nabe restaurants of Ryōgoku surround it.

sights.n: Sumida Hokusai Museum (すみだ北斎美術館)
sights.w: Kazuyo Sejima's faceted aluminium museum (2016) for Hokusai, who spent most of his 88 years in Sumida — his life, his prints and the neighbourhood that shaped them.
Meiji-era stroll garden built by the Iwasaki (Mitsubishi) family — a big pond, stepping stones of prized rock from across Japan, carp, turtles and a lakeside teahouse.
Edo-period shrine in old-town Yanesen with a tunnel of small vermilion torii and a hillside of some 3,000 azaleas each April.

sights.n: Shibuya Scramble Crossing (渋谷スクランブル交差点)
sights.w: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing — up to 3,000 people per green light outside Shibuya Station and the Hachikō statue; watch it from Shibuya Sky or the station's upper floors.
Big, informal park beside Meiji Jingū — weekend buskers, rockabilly dancers, ginkgo avenues in autumn and festivals on the event plaza.

sights.n: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (新宿御苑)
sights.w: Former imperial garden blending French formal, English landscape and Japanese styles — 1,000 cherry trees, a tropical greenhouse and a teahouse, minutes from Shinjuku Station.

sights.n: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (東京都庁)
sights.w: Kenzo Tange's twin-towered city hall with free 202 m observation decks — Mt Fuji on clear winter mornings and an evening projection-mapping show on the facade.

sights.n: Shinjuku Golden Gai (新宿ゴールデン街)
sights.w: Six narrow lanes of 200-odd postwar shoebox bars, each seating a handful — the most atmospheric drinking quarter in Tokyo.
Shrine to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken in a 70-hectare planted forest between Harajuku and Yoyogi — giant cypress torii, sake-barrel wall, and Japan's busiest New Year hatsumōde.

sights.n: Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー)
sights.w: At 634 m the world's tallest tower — observation decks at 350 m and 450 m, with Tokyo Solamachi mall and an aquarium at its foot.
Yanagisawa Yoshiyasu's 1702 stroll garden recreating 88 scenes from waka poetry — a weeping cherry in spring and lantern-lit maples in autumn.
Tokyo's oldest daimyō garden (1629, Mito Tokugawa) — the Engetsu-kyō full-moon bridge, plum grove and miniature Chinese and Japanese landscapes beside Tokyo Dome.
Tokyo's grand kabuki theatre behind a Momoyama-style facade — buy a single-act makumi ticket on the day to sample a play from the top gallery.
The 1911 granite bridge at 'kilometre zero' of Japan's roads — the start of the Edo-period Tōkaidō, bronze kirin on its lamps, the expressway overhead soon to be buried.
Shōgun's former duck-hunting garden on Tokyo Bay with a tidal seawater pond and the Nakajima teahouse for matcha, ringed by Shiodome towers.
The Tokugawa shōguns' family temple — the 1622 Sangedatsumon gate, rows of jizō statues in knitted caps, and Tokyo Tower rising directly behind the main hall.

sights.n: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower — Tokyo City View & Mori Art Museum
sights.w: The 54-storey heart of Roppongi Hills: the Mori Art Museum's contemporary shows and the Tokyo City View deck on the 52nd floor.
sights.k: Mori Art Museum, Tokyo City View

sights.w: Barefoot immersive digital-art museum in Toyosu — wade knee-deep through projected koi, a floating-flower dome and a mirrored infinity crystal universe.
Tokyo's wholesale fish market since 2018 — watch the dawn tuna auction from the observation gallery, then sushi breakfast in the market restaurants.
Fukagawa's great Hachiman shrine — birthplace of Edo kanjin sumo (the yokozuna monument stands here) and host of the water-splashing Fukagawa Hachiman festival.
Japan's major public contemporary-art museum, in Kiba Park near Kiyosumi-Shirakawa's coffee roasters.

sights.n: Nakano Broadway (中野ブロードウェイ)
sights.w: 1966 shopping-and-apartment complex turned otaku mecca — four floors of Mandarake, vintage toys, manga, idol goods and watch dealers at the end of Nakano Sun Mall.
Tokyo's bohemian village of vintage-clothing shops, tiny theatres, live houses and coffee stands around Shimo-kitazawa Station and the Ichibangai shopping street.
The 333 m orange-and-white 1958 lattice tower — Main Deck at 150 m and Top Deck at 250 m, and still the city's favourite night-skyline icon.
Small Takanawa temple holding the graves of the 47 rōnin of Akō — incense is still lit at each grave, and a festival marks their vendetta every 14 December.

sights.n: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka (三鷹の森ジブリ美術館)
sights.w: Hayao Miyazaki's own whimsical museum on the edge of Inokashira Park — animation workshops, a Catbus room, a rooftop Laputa robot and short films shown only here. Advance tickets only.
Kichijōji's beloved park — swan boats on a cherry-lined pond, the Benzaiten shrine and weekend craft stalls, a short walk from the Ghibli Museum.
599 m sacred mountain an hour from Shinjuku — cable car or trails up to Yakuō-in temple and a summit view of Mt Fuji on clear days.
Tokyo's second-oldest temple (733) in a spring-fed forest, ringed by soba shops making Jindai-ji soba from the local water.

sights.n: Great Buddha of Kamakura — Kōtoku-in (鎌倉大仏)
sights.w: The 13.35 m bronze Amida Buddha (1252) sitting in the open air since a 15th-century tsunami washed its hall away — you can step inside the hollow statue.
Kamakura's central shrine, founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo — a grand approach from the sea up Dankazura, lotus ponds and a hilltop main hall.
Tokugawa Ieyasu's lavishly carved mausoleum shrine in cedar forest — the Yōmeimon gate, the three wise monkeys and the sleeping cat; part of the UNESCO Shrines and Temples of Nikkō.
Daikyō-ji, the shitamachi temple of the 'Tora-san' films — its halls wrapped in astonishing wood-carved panels, reached down the Taishakuten-sandō street of kusa-dango and senbei shops.

sights.n: Kasai Rinkai Park (葛西臨海公園)
sights.w: Bayside park with a giant Ferris wheel, a bird sanctuary, a beach and the Tokyo Sea Life Park aquarium's tuna doughnut tank.

sights.n: Holy Resurrection Cathedral — Nikolai-dō (ニコライ堂)
sights.w: Green-domed 1891 Byzantine-style Orthodox cathedral founded by St Nicholas of Japan, rising unexpectedly over Ochanomizu.

sights.n: Tokyo International Forum (東京国際フォーラム)
sights.w: Rafael Viñoly's 1996 glass-hull atrium between Yūrakuchō and Tokyo Station — free to walk through, with a weekend antique market on the plaza.

sights.n: Shibuya Sky — Shibuya Scramble Square (渋谷スカイ)
sights.w: Open-air rooftop deck 230 m above the Scramble Crossing on top of the 2019 Shibuya Scramble Square tower — sunset over Mt Fuji is the prize.
Bronze of the Akita who waited at Shibuya Station for his dead master for nearly ten years — Tokyo's most famous meeting point.

sights.n: Yebisu Garden Place (恵比寿ガーデンプレイス)
sights.w: Plaza on the site of the old Yebisu brewery — the beer's birthplace brewery restarted here, plus the Tokyo Photographic Art Museum and a Baccarat chandelier each winter.
Tadao Ando's spiral-ramp mall on the zelkova-lined Omotesandō boulevard — the avenue of architect-designed flagships between Harajuku and Aoyama.
Kengo Kuma's bamboo-lined museum of pre-modern Asian art (Kōrin's Irises screen each spring) with a deep, hilly stroll garden and teahouses behind.

sights.n: The National Art Center, Tokyo (国立新美術館)
sights.w: Kisho Kurokawa's undulating glass-facade exhibition hall in Roppongi — Japan's largest exhibition space, no permanent collection, a cone-top café.

sights.n: Kyū-Shiba-rikyū Gardens (旧芝離宮恩賜庭園)
sights.w: One of Tokyo's oldest daimyō stroll gardens (1678), a pond landscape tucked beside Hamamatsuchō Station.

sights.n: Rainbow Bridge (レインボーブリッジ)
sights.w: Suspension bridge to Odaiba with a free pedestrian promenade on each side — the classic view back to the Tokyo skyline and Tokyo Tower, lit at night.

sights.n: National Museum of Western Art (国立西洋美術館)
sights.w: Le Corbusier's only building in East Asia — part of the UNESCO Le Corbusier serial site — housing the Matsukata collection of Rodin, Monet and Old Masters; Rodin's Gates of Hell stand in the forecourt.
Josiah Conder's 1896 Jacobean-style mansion for the Mitsubishi Iwasaki family, with a Japanese wing and a Swiss-chalet billiard house — Meiji Westernisation in one garden.
Leafy old cemetery of shōguns' retainers and Meiji notables — cherry-tree avenues, the last shōgun Tokugawa Yoshinobu's tomb and the neighbourhood's resident cats.
The 1649 Gongen-style shrine beside Sensō-ji honouring the temple's three founders, home of the riotous Sanja Matsuri each May.
Josiah Conder's stone Western villa above a terraced rose garden that steps down to a Japanese pond garden by Ogawa Jihei — spectacular at the May and October rose festivals.

sights.n: Sunshine City, Ikebukuro (サンシャインシティ)
sights.w: Ikebukuro's mega-complex — the rooftop Sunshine Aquarium with its 'sky penguins', Namjatown, the Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo and the Sunshine 60 observatory — next to Otome Road.

sights.n: Jiyū Gakuen Myōnichikan (自由学園明日館)
sights.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1921 Prairie-style school building with Arata Endo — an Important Cultural Property where you can take tea in the double-height hall.

sights.n: Meguro Parasitological Museum (目黒寄生虫館)
sights.w: Free, gloriously odd private museum of some 300 parasite specimens — the star is an 8.8 m tapeworm.

sights.n: Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum (東京都庭園美術館)
sights.w: Prince Asaka's 1933 Art Deco residence — Lalique glass doors, Henri Rapin interiors — used as an exhibition museum inside a Japanese and Western garden.
The 'cat temple' said to be the birthplace of the maneki-neko — thousands of white beckoning cats lined up beside the hall, under a 22.5 m three-tiered pagoda.
Hilltop head temple of Nichiren Buddhism on the site where Nichiren died in 1282 — with the oldest five-storey pagoda in the Kantō region.

sights.n: CupNoodles Museum Yokohama (カップヌードルミュージアム 横浜)
sights.w: Momofuku Ando's instant-noodle museum in Minato Mirai — design your own Cup Noodle to take home, or hand-make chicken ramen from scratch.

sights.n: Yokohama Landmark Tower — Sky Garden (横浜ランドマークタワー)
sights.w: Minato Mirai's 296 m tower with the Sky Garden observatory on the 69th floor over Yokohama Bay, Mt Fuji on clear days.
Cedar-shaded shrine on Lake Ashi whose red 'torii of peace' stands in the water — the classic Hakone photograph.

sights.n: Hakone Open-Air Museum (彫刻の森美術館)
sights.w: Japan's first open-air art museum — Moore and Rodin on mountain lawns, a stained-glass Symphonic Sculpture tower, a Picasso pavilion and a hot-spring foot bath.
Hillside temple of the 9 m eleven-headed Kannon, with sea views over Yuigahama, a cave of carved deities and a famous hydrangea path in June.
Second of Kamakura's Five Great Zen Temples (1282), a forested complex by Kita-Kamakura Station holding the National Treasure Shariden relic hall.
Japan's oldest Zen training monastery (1253) and first of Kamakura's Five Mountains — great gate, juniper garden and a hike up to Hansōbō's tengu statues.
Small Zen temple behind a grove of 2,000 Mōsō bamboo, with matcha served in a tea pavilion inside the grove.
Tidal island off Shōnan's surf beaches — Enoshima Shrine, the Sea Candle lighthouse, the Iwaya caves and shirasu-don stalls, with Mt Fuji across Sagami Bay.
97 m waterfall draining Lake Chūzenji — an elevator drops to a platform at the base of the plunge; ranked among Japan's three finest falls.
Nikkō's chief Tendai temple, founded by Shōdō Shōnin — three giant gilded Buddhas in the Sanbutsu-dō and the Taiyūin mausoleum of the third shōgun; part of the UNESCO Nikkō site.
High lake at the foot of sacred Mt Nantai, ringed by autumn colour, old embassy villas and Chūzen-ji temple — reached by the hairpin Irohazaka road.

sights.n: Chūreitō Pagoda — Arakurayama Sengen Park (忠霊塔)
sights.w: The five-storey pagoda framed against Mt Fuji — 398 steps up from Shimoyoshida; cherry blossom in April and autumn maples make it Japan's most-photographed view.
The most accessible of the Fuji Five Lakes — Fuji reflected on the north shore, the Kachi Kachi ropeway and lakeside onsen ryokan.
Eight crystal spring ponds fed by Fuji snowmelt in a thatched-roof village between Kawaguchiko and Yamanakako.
Kawagoe's great Tendai temple — rooms moved from Edo Castle (including Iemitsu's birth chamber) and the 540 Gohyaku Rakan stone disciples, each face different.

sights.n: Toki no Kane — Kawagoe Time Bell (時の鐘)
sights.w: Wooden bell tower rising over the kurazukuri clay-walled merchant houses of 'Little Edo' — still rung four times a day.

sights.n: Yayoi Kusama Museum (草間彌生美術館)
sights.w: Five-storey white museum devoted to Kusama — polka dots, pumpkins and an infinity-mirror room; timed tickets sell out in advance.
Shinjuku's guardian shrine beside Golden Gai — the Tori-no-Ichi rake fairs in November and a Sunday antique market under the trees.

sights.n: Tokyu Kabukichō Tower (東急歌舞伎町タワー)
sights.w: 2023 entertainment tower in the heart of Kabukichō — theatre, a neon 'Shinjuku Kabuki Hall' food hall of yokochō stalls and rooftop views; the Godzilla head looms next door.
Sloping old geisha quarter with cobbled back alleys of ryōtei, a French-expat bistro scene and Zenkoku-ji's Bishamonten at its crest.
Startling 1934 Indian-style Buddhist temple by Itō Chūta, with a pipe organ inside and a breakfast café — at the gate of the Tsukiji outer market.
Nihonbashi shrine for safe childbirth — expectant parents queue on the 'Day of the Dog'; Ningyōchō's ningyō-yaki stalls are a block away.
The 1932 neo-Renaissance Seiko clock tower on the Ginza 4-chōme crossing — Ginza's emblem since the Shōwa era, with luxury floors below.
Tokyo's largest waterside park — poplar avenues along the Koaidame reservoir, a metasequoia forest and 200,000 irises in June.

sights.n: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum (江戸東京たてもの園)
sights.w: Thirty rescued historic buildings in Koganei Park — Edo farmhouses, a Shōwa sentō and shop row that inspired Spirited Away, and Maekawa Kunio's modernist home.

sights.n: Shōwa Kinen Park (国営昭和記念公園)
sights.w: Vast national memorial park in Tachikawa — seasonal flower fields (tulips, cosmos), a golden ginkgo avenue, a Japanese garden and bike paths.
The largest limestone cave in the Kantō, deep in the Okutama mountains — a steady 11 °C walk past stalactites and a lit 'Hall of the Gods'.

Punk-and-vintage Chūō Line neighbourhood of used-clothing shops, tiny live houses, izakaya under the tracks and the huge Awa-odori dance festival every August — named one of the world's coolest neighbourhoods by Time Out in 2026.

sights.n: Nakameguro & the Meguro River (中目黒・目黒川)
sights.w: Canal-side neighbourhood of boutiques, coffee bars and izakaya under the tracks; in early April 800 cherry trees arch over the Meguro River and the lanterns come out.
Genteel residential shopping town famed for patisseries and the 'Sweets Forest' dessert hall, plus La Vita's mini-Venice canal.

sights.n: Meguro Sky Garden (目黒天空庭園)
sights.w: A looping rooftop park built on top of the Ōhashi expressway junction — 7,000 m² of gardens 35 m up, with sunset views toward Fuji.
Shōgun Tsunayoshi's 1681 temple for his mother — one of the few great Edo-period halls to survive earthquake and war intact, quiet and rarely visited.

sights.n: Tokyo Dome City (東京ドームシティ)
sights.w: Home of the Yomiuri Giants (55,000 seats) plus a roller coaster that threads through a building, the LaQua spa and the Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame.
Black-lacquered Confucian temple founded by the shōguns' Confucian scholars — the Edo academy where samurai officials were trained; giant bronze Confucius in the grounds.
Silk merchant Hara Sankei's stroll garden of historic buildings moved from Kyoto, Kamakura and Gifu — a three-storey pagoda over the pond and a gasshō farmhouse.
Japan's largest Chinatown — ten ornate gates, the Kantei-byō and Ma Zu temples and 500-odd shops steaming nikuman and xiaolongbao.
Japan's first Western-style park (1903), across the moat from the Imperial Palace — rose beds, an open-air concert hall and the century-old Matsumoto-rō restaurant.
The stepped-pyramid granite parliament (1936) — free guided tours of the House of Councillors chamber run on weekdays.
Wooded former Edo Castle enclosure north of the palace — the Budōkan, the Science Museum and MOMAT among cherry trees by the Chidorigafuchi moat.
Postwar black-market street under the Yamanote tracks between Ueno and Okachimachi — fishmongers shouting year-end deals, dried goods, spices, sneakers and standing izakaya.
'Memory Lane' — a smoky postwar alley of yakitori and motsu-yaki counters squeezed against the tracks at Shinjuku's west exit.
Harajuku's 400 m teen-fashion street opposite the station — crêpes, kawaii shops, rainbow candy floss and weekend crowds shoulder to shoulder.

sights.n: Katsushika Shibamata Tora-san Museum (葛飾柴又寅さん記念館)
sights.w: Museum of the 48-film 'Otoko wa Tsurai yo' saga — the Kurumaya dango shop set and props from the films shot in Shibamata from 1969 to 1995.

sights.n: KochiKame Museum, Kameari (こち亀記念館)
sights.w: Compact museum for Osamu Akimoto's 200-volume manga 'KochiKame: Tokyo Beat Cops', recreating the Kameari Park police box — start of a trail of bronze statues of Ryōtsu and friends around Kameari Station.
Sōji-ji, the great Shingon temple of Adachi (founded 826) — peony gardens, kusa-dango stalls at the gate and a February daruma-burning rite.
